newsitem.title: UK: Grand Met to pay interim dividend as FID.
newsitem.headline: Grand Met to pay interim dividend as FID.

text.p: British food and drink group Grand Metropolitan Plc said on Thursday that in the light of changes in the budget, it intends to pay its interim dividend in respect of the year to September 30, 1997 as a foreign income dividend (FID).
The net dividend of 6.25 pence per shares was announced on May 12 and will be paid on October 6, 1997.

"The advantage of paying a FID is that the company is able to recover from the Inland Revenue Advance Corporation Tax (ACT) on the dividend where, in broad terms, the dividend can be matched with repatriated overseas profits on which overseas tax has been paid," the company said in a statement.
It said this was particularly attractive for Grand Metropolitan as its generates a high level of its profits overseas.
It said that by treating the interim dividend as a FID, the group will be able to recover around 33 million stg in ACT.

The changes made in the July 2 budget "reduce the value of conventional dividends in the hands of UK pension funds and certain other investors which are no longer able to reclaim the tax credits on such dividends," the company added.
Also, from April 6, 1999, companies will no longer be able to elect to pay dividends as FIDs.
